# Scoped ignore list for the frontend image scan ONLY (passed explicitly
# via trivy-action's `trivyignores` input on the security-container-frontend
# job in ci.yml, its twin in scheduled-security-scan.yml, and release.yml's
# scan of the published digest) -- NOT a repo-root .trivyignore, so it can't
# accidentally suppress a real finding in the backend image scan.
#
# This file is currently EMPTY of entries, deliberately.
#
# It previously suppressed three findings against the
# nginx-unprivileged:1-alpine3.23 base: CVE-2026-33630 (c-ares
# use-after-free) and CVE-2026-5773 / CVE-2026-6276 (curl), each with a
# note to remove it "once nginxinc publishes a rebuilt digest". The base
# has since moved to the 1-alpine3.24 line (frontend/Dockerfile), which
# carries newer Alpine packages across the board -- the two curl entries
# were demonstrably obsolete (the eight *unsuppressed* curl CVEs that had
# been failing the scan need 8.22.0-r0, well past the 8.20.0-r0 that fixed
# these two), and a suppression cannot tell you whether it is still doing
# anything, so all three were dropped rather than carried forward against
# an unexamined base. The scan is green without them.
#
# Adding an entry back: one CVE ID per line, each with a written
# justification above it covering (a) why no fixed base image is available
# to re-pin to instead, and (b) why the vulnerable code path is unreachable
# in this deployment -- this image only serves static built assets via
# nginx (frontend/nginx.conf has no `resolver` and no `proxy_pass`, so no
# runtime DNS resolution and no upstream calls), runs unprivileged, and its
# own scripts (docker-entrypoint-runtime-config.sh, the HEALTHCHECK) use
# `wget` and `envsubst`, never `curl`. Prefer re-pinning the base over
# adding an entry: a suppression outlives the release that needed it.
